subject: social_science
chapter_title: The Constitution of India -- An Introduction

concepts.title: Meaning and Purpose of a Constitution
concepts.definition: A constitution is a written document that lays down the basic rules and principles according to which a country is governed, defining the structure of government and the rights and duties of citizens.
concepts.key_idea: A constitution is the supreme law that defines how a country is governed and protects the rights of its citizens.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: define a constitution and explain its importance
why does a country need a constitution
what are the main functions of a constitution
how does a constitution protect the rights of citizens
list the key purposes served by a constitution

solution_steps.explain: A constitution is a set of written rules and principles that govern a country and define the relationship between the government and citizens.
It lays down the structure of government, distributes powers among organs, and guarantees fundamental rights to citizens.
By limiting the power of government and protecting rights, a constitution ensures that the country is governed by law and not by arbitrary decisions.

worked_examples.question: What is a constitution? Why is it important?
worked_examples.solution: A constitution is a document of basic rules and principles according to which a country is governed. It is important because it defines the structure of government, limits its powers and protects citizens' rights.
worked_examples.answer: A constitution is the supreme law governing a country; it structures government and protects rights.

worked_examples.question: State any three functions of a constitution.
worked_examples.solution: A constitution defines the structure of government, distributes powers among the legislature, executive and judiciary, and guarantees fundamental rights to citizens.
worked_examples.answer: A constitution structures government, distributes powers and protects rights.

exercises.question: Define constitution and state its importance.

concepts.title: The Making of the Indian Constitution
concepts.definition: The Indian Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly over a period of about three years, drawing on discussions, debates and the study of constitutions of other countries, and was adopted on 26 November 1949.
concepts.key_idea: The Indian Constitution was made by the Constituent Assembly through discussion and consensus, and came into effect on 26 January 1950.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: describe how the Indian Constitution was made
who framed the Indian Constitution and how long did it take
on which date was the Indian Constitution adopted and when did it come into force
what sources inspired the makers of the Indian Constitution
why did the making of the Constitution take a long time

solution_steps.explain: The Indian Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly, whose members were elected to represent the people of India.
The Assembly held discussions and debates over nearly three years, examining drafts and studying the constitutions of other countries.
The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into effect on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

worked_examples.question: How was the Indian Constitution made?
worked_examples.solution: The Indian Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly through long discussions and debates over about three years, and was adopted on 26 November 1949.
worked_examples.answer: The Constituent Assembly framed the Constitution through debate over three years, adopted on 26 November 1949.

worked_examples.question: When did the Indian Constitution come into force and what is this day called?
worked_examples.solution: The Indian Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, a day celebrated every year as Republic Day.
worked_examples.answer: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day.

exercises.question: Describe how the Indian Constitution was made.
When was the Indian Constitution adopted and when did it come into force?
Why did the making of the Constitution take a long time?

concepts.title: The Constituent Assembly
concepts.definition: The Constituent Assembly was the body of elected representatives that drafted the Indian Constitution, with Dr Rajendra Prasad as its President and Dr B R Ambedkar as the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.
concepts.key_idea: The Constituent Assembly, led by Dr Rajendra Prasad and with Dr B R Ambedkar as Chairman of the Drafting Committee, drafted the Indian Constitution.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: what was the Constituent Assembly and who were its key members
who was the President of the Constituent Assembly
who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and why is he called the Father of the Constitution
how were the members of the Constituent Assembly chosen
what was the role of the Drafting Committee in making the Constitution

solution_steps.explain: The Constituent Assembly was an elected body of representatives that was formed to draft the Constitution of India.
Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Assembly and Dr B R Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee.

solution_steps.action: explain the role of the Drafting Committee
solution_steps.explain: The Drafting Committee, under Dr B R Ambedkar, prepared the written draft of the Constitution, which is why he is called the Father of the Indian Constitution.

worked_examples.question: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
worked_examples.solution: Dr B R Ambedkar was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee and is known as the Father of the Indian Constitution.
worked_examples.answer: Dr B R Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee and is the Father of the Constitution.

worked_examples.question: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
worked_examples.solution: Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the Indian Constitution.
worked_examples.answer: Dr Rajendra Prasad was the President of the Constituent Assembly.

exercises.question: What was the Constituent Assembly? Who was its President?

concepts.title: The Preamble and Its Significance
concepts.definition: The Preamble is the introductory statement of the Constitution that declares India to be a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic and states the goals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
concepts.key_idea: The Preamble is the introduction to the Constitution that summarises its aims and the values on which the Indian Republic is built.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: what is the Preamble and why is it important
list the key words used in the Preamble to describe India
what values and goals are mentioned in the Preamble
explain the meaning of sovereign and secular as used in the Preamble
why is the Preamble called the soul of the Constitution

solution_steps.explain: The Preamble is the opening statement of the Constitution that introduces its purposes and principles.
The Preamble describes India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
It promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity to all citizens, which is why it is called the soul of the Constitution.

worked_examples.question: What is the Preamble? State its importance.
worked_examples.solution: The Preamble is the introductory part of the Constitution that states its aims and values. It is important because it declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic and promises justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
worked_examples.answer: The Preamble introduces the Constitution's aims; it declares India a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

worked_examples.question: Explain the terms Sovereign and Secular as used in the Preamble.
worked_examples.solution: Sovereign means India is free to take its own decisions without external control, and Secular means the state does not promote any one religion and treats all religions equally.
worked_examples.answer: Sovereign: India is independent; Secular: state treats all religions equally.

exercises.question: What is the Preamble? Why is it important?

concepts.title: Fundamental Rights
concepts.definition: Fundamental Rights are the basic rights guaranteed to all citizens by the Constitution, including the right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
concepts.key_idea: Fundamental Rights are the six basic rights guaranteed by the Constitution to all citizens and protected by the courts.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: what are Fundamental Rights and why are they important
list the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed by the Indian Constitution
explain the right to equality and give an example
what is the right to constitutional remedies and why is it important
how do Fundamental Rights protect citizens from misuse of power

solution_steps.explain: Fundamental Rights are the basic rights guaranteed to all citizens by the Constitution and enforceable by the courts.
The six Fundamental Rights are: right to equality, right to freedom, right against exploitation, right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and right to constitutional remedies.
These rights protect citizens from arbitrary action by the government and allow them to approach the courts if their rights are violated.

worked_examples.question: What are Fundamental Rights? Name any three of them.
worked_examples.solution: Fundamental Rights are the basic rights guaranteed by the Constitution to all citizens. Three of them are the right to equality, the right to freedom, and the right against exploitation.
worked_examples.answer: Fundamental Rights are constitutionally guaranteed basic rights; examples include equality, freedom and against exploitation.

worked_examples.question: Why is the right to constitutional remedies important?
worked_examples.solution: The right to constitutional remedies allows citizens to approach the courts if any of their Fundamental Rights are violated, which makes all other rights meaningful and enforceable.
worked_examples.answer: It lets citizens approach courts to enforce their Fundamental Rights.

exercises.question: What are Fundamental Rights? Why are they important?

concepts.title: Directive Principles of State Policy
concepts.definition: Directive Principles of State Policy are guidelines laid down in the Constitution for the government to follow in making laws and policies, aimed at establishing social and economic justice and reducing inequalities in society.
concepts.key_idea: Directive Principles are instructions to the government to work towards social and economic justice; they are not enforceable by courts but are fundamental to governance.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: what are Directive Principles of State Policy
how do Directive Principles differ from Fundamental Rights
what is the main aim of the Directive Principles
are Directive Principles enforceable by courts and why
give two examples of Directive Principles

solution_steps.explain: Directive Principles are guidelines in the Constitution that direct the government to make policies for social and economic welfare.
Their aim is to reduce inequalities, provide adequate means of livelihood, and ensure social and economic justice for all citizens.
Unlike Fundamental Rights, Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts, but they are fundamental to the governance of the country.

worked_examples.question: What are Directive Principles of State Policy?
worked_examples.solution: Directive Principles are guidelines given in the Constitution that direct the government to make laws and policies aimed at social and economic justice.
worked_examples.answer: Directive Principles guide the government towards social and economic justice.

worked_examples.question: How do Directive Principles differ from Fundamental Rights?
worked_examples.solution: Fundamental Rights are enforceable by courts and protect individual rights, while Directive Principles are not enforceable by courts but guide the government in making policies for welfare.
worked_examples.answer: Fundamental Rights are enforceable; Directive Principles are guidelines not enforceable by courts.

exercises.question: What are Directive Principles of State Policy?

concepts.title: Fundamental Duties
concepts.definition: Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of citizens towards the country listed in the Constitution, including respect for the national symbols, protecting the environment, and promoting harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
concepts.key_idea: Fundamental Duties are the duties of citizens towards the nation that complement the Fundamental Rights they enjoy.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: what are Fundamental Duties and why are they important
list any four Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens
how are Fundamental Duties related to Fundamental Rights
why should citizens respect the national flag and anthem
what duty do citizens have towards the environment

solution_steps.explain: Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of citizens towards the country listed in the Constitution.
They include respecting the national flag and anthem, protecting the environment, safeguarding public property and promoting harmony.
Fundamental Duties remind citizens that rights and duties go together; enjoying rights requires performing duties towards the nation.

worked_examples.question: What are Fundamental Duties? Give two examples.
worked_examples.solution: Fundamental Duties are the moral obligations of citizens towards the country. Two examples are respecting the national flag and anthem and protecting the environment.
worked_examples.answer: Fundamental Duties are citizens' obligations; examples include respecting national symbols and protecting the environment.

worked_examples.question: How are Fundamental Duties related to Fundamental Rights?
worked_examples.solution: Fundamental Duties complement Fundamental Rights; while rights protect citizens, duties remind them of their responsibilities towards the nation and society.
worked_examples.answer: Rights and duties are complementary; duties balance the rights citizens enjoy.

exercises.question: What are Fundamental Duties? Why are they important?
List any four Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens.
Explain the relationship between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.

concepts.title: Features of the Indian Constitution
concepts.definition: The Indian Constitution is a written, lengthy and detailed document that establishes a federal system with unitary features, provides for a parliamentary government, includes Fundamental Rights and Duties, and can be amended to meet changing needs.
concepts.key_idea: The Indian Constitution is a written, federal yet unitary, parliamentary and flexible document that protects rights and can be amended.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: list the main features of the Indian Constitution
why is the Indian Constitution called a lengthy document
explain the federal nature of the Indian Constitution with unitary features
what is meant by a written and flexible constitution
how does the Constitution provide for a parliamentary form of government

solution_steps.explain: The Indian Constitution is written, lengthy, federal with unitary features, and provides for a parliamentary form of government.
It divides powers between the centre and states (federal) but gives strong powers to the centre during emergencies (unitary).
The Constitution can be amended to meet changing needs, which makes it both rigid in basic structure and flexible in detail.

worked_examples.question: State any four features of the Indian Constitution.
worked_examples.solution: The Indian Constitution is written and lengthy, establishes a federal system with unitary features, provides for a parliamentary government, and guarantees Fundamental Rights and Duties.
worked_examples.answer: Features: written, federal with unitary features, parliamentary government, Fundamental Rights and Duties.

worked_examples.question: Why is the Indian Constitution called a federal constitution with unitary features?
worked_examples.solution: It is federal because it divides powers between the centre and the states, but it is unitary in spirit because the centre has strong powers, especially during emergencies.
worked_examples.answer: It divides powers (federal) but gives strong powers to the centre (unitary).

exercises.question: List any five features of the Indian Constitution.

concepts.title: Secularism and the Indian Constitution
concepts.definition: Secularism in the Indian Constitution means that the state does not promote any one religion as the official religion and treats all religions equally, allowing every citizen to profess, practise and propagate any religion of their choice.
concepts.key_idea: India is a secular state where the government treats all religions equally and citizens are free to follow any religion.
question_patterns: in Class 7 civics: what is secularism as provided by the Indian Constitution
how does the Constitution ensure freedom of religion to citizens
why is India called a secular state
differentiate between a secular state and a state with an official religion
what does the right to freedom of religion include

solution_steps.explain: Secularism means the state does not have an official religion and treats all religions equally.
The Constitution gives every citizen the right to profess, practise and propagate any religion of their choice.
India is secular because the government does not favour any religion and allows all citizens to follow their faith freely.

worked_examples.question: What is secularism according to the Indian Constitution?
worked_examples.solution: Secularism means the state does not promote any one religion and treats all religions equally, giving citizens freedom to follow any religion.
worked_examples.answer: Secularism: state treats all religions equally and grants freedom of religion.

worked_examples.question: Why is India called a secular state?
worked_examples.solution: India is called a secular state because the government does not have an official religion and allows all citizens to practise, profess and propagate any religion freely.
worked_examples.answer: India is secular because it has no official religion and grants freedom of religion.
